title: Rust: CSV Data Processing
description: Parse and analyze CSV data in Rust.

steps.title: Parse CSV Row
steps.description: Write a function `parse_csv_row(row: &str) -> Vec<&str>` that splits a CSV row by commas. Test with `"Alice,30,Engineer"`.
hints: Trim whitespace from each field: `.map(|s| s.trim())`.
Print each field on its own line.

verification.failureMessage: Parse and print fields from the CSV row.

steps.title: Parse Multi-Row CSV
steps.description:
Write a function `parse_csv(data: &str) -> Vec<Vec<&str>>` that parses a full CSV string (multiple rows). Test with:
`"Name,Age,City
Alice,30,NYC
Bob,25,LA
Charlie,35,Chicago"`
hints: Skip the header line or include it.

verification.failureMessage: Parse and print all 3 data rows.

steps.title: Extract Column
steps.description: Write a function `get_column(csv: &str, col_index: usize) -> Vec<&str>` that extracts a column by index. Print the Age column (index 1) from the CSV above.
hints: Parse the CSV first, then skip the header.

verification.failureMessage: Extract and print the Age column.

steps.title: CSV to Struct
steps.description: Define a struct `Person { name: String, age: i32, city: String }`. Write `rows_to_persons(rows: Vec<Vec<&str>>) -> Vec<Person>`. Parse and print the people.
hints: Iterate over rows, skipping the header.
Print each person with `println!("{}, {}, {}", p.name, p.age, p.city)`

verification.failureMessage: Convert CSV rows to Person structs and print.

steps.title: CSV Statistics
steps.description:
Given a CSV of sales data: `"Product,Price,Quantity
Widget,10.99,5
Gadget,24.99,3
Doohickey,5.99,8"`, calculate total revenue (sum of Price * Quantity). Print each product's revenue and the total.
hints: Parse each row into a struct with price and quantity.

verification.failureMessage: Print each product's revenue and the total.
